title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

reports.title: Sisters sue Española over traffic stop they say was illegal

summary:
Two Rio Arriba County sisters are suing the city of Española over a July 23 traffic stop. Jaclynn Gonzales, 21, was driving with her 12-year-old sister when a Flock Safety camera misread their license plate, confusing a final 2 for a 7 and matching a stolen car from Rio Rancho. Police stopped them on Calle Duran, handcuffed both, and placed them in separate patrol cars before discovering the error. Jaclynn asked officers to call their mother, who lived nearby, to pick up the girl, but officers instead handcuffed the child and put her in another police vehicle.

The lawsuits, filed Jan. 3 by attorney Sheri Raphaelson, seek unspecified damages for anxiety, fear, and restriction of movement. Raphaelson also represents Adam Pacheco, a 17-year-old honor student who was stopped and made to kneel after a similar mistaken alert in April. The city of Española, Police Chief Mizel A. Garcia, and Flock Safety did not respond to requests for comment, so no further court dates or responses are described.
